history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Pali city - it stands at Ranakpur in Desuri tehsil, Pali district, adjacent to the Ranakpur Jain temple complex, about 90 km from Pali city. The Surya Narayan Temple dates to the 13th century - two centuries before the Jain complex - was desecrated in the period of invasions, and was reconstructed with the rest of the complex in the 15th century. It is managed by the Udaipur (Mewar) royal family trust. Built of white marble in the Nagara style, its sanctum follows a circular/octagonal plan with projecting bays; the highlight is the idol of the Sun God on his seven-horse chariot. Walls, ceilings, and pillars carry fine carvings of warriors, horses, and celestial figures in excellent condition. The temple faces east with a shikhara over the sanctum; nearby are the Amba Mata shrine and the Jain complex. town_description: Ranakpur is a small village in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, nestled in a quiet valley of the Aravalli Range on the banks of the Maghai (Mavi) river. It is one of India's great Jain pilgrimage centres, surrounded by forested hills; the nearest railhead is Falna and the nearest airports are Udaipur and Jodhpur.

travel.road: On the Jodhpur-Udaipur highway via Sadri/Desuri; buses and taxis from Falna, Udaipur, and Jodhpur.
